description: We are Cedar Pulse, a team of curious students from Lebanon who love space, coding and electronics.
summary:
We’re Cedar Pulse, from CNDL.
Meet ORBI, a floating AI camera that watches over astronauts’ physical and mental health.
With its thermal and RGB eyes, ORBI tracks sleep, exercise, mood, heart rate and posture, around the clock.
It compares this data with each astronaut’s health records to catch problems early, alert the crew in emergencies, and support their mental well-being.

Your body. Your mission. Your guardian.
details:
ORBI & Orbital: watching over the body and the mind on the way to Mars

On a mission to Mars, help is far away. A message to Earth takes about 20 minutes each way, the journey lasts six months each way, and there will be no psychologist on board. NASA lists behavioral changes and psychiatric disorders among the official risks of long missions. The Mars-500 simulation showed how slowly and silently these problems appear: the crew moved less, slept badly, and one member drifted into a 25-hour day. Today, an astronaut’s body is monitored continuously, but the mind is only checked now and then.

Our answer has two parts. ORBI is a floating AI camera that follows each astronaut like a quiet companion. Its RGB camera reads heart rate, facial expression, posture and fatigue. Its thermal camera reads breathing, temperature and signs of stress, even in the dark. Everything ORBI detects is sent automatically to Orbital, our AI software. Orbital compares each day with the astronaut’s previous days and with a database of earlier health data. It detects problems early and suggests solutions, and it alerts the crew only when the situation is serious. Everything runs on board, with no need to wait for Earth.

What makes it original is that mental health is a core signal, not an add-on. The system is passive, so there’s nothing to wear and no forms to fill in. Each astronaut is compared with their own normal. And because privacy is built in, ORBI acts as a companion, not a supervisor.
